dataset.description:
The description is created to publicly outline the following: 

1. What data including metadata will be created?
Answer: Feed recipe (semi-protected for IPR), Ingredient and pellet Biochemistry, Pellet water stability, Fish feeding trial (fish biometric, biomass, feed input), Feed conversion ratio data will be posted. Protocol of extrusion, experiments and analyses will be accompanied with the data as metadata.

2. How the data will be created, handled, and stored?
Answer: The data will be created in .docx or .xlsx format, also video to prove activities of extrusion. The data will be shared between the Principlal investigator (Dr. Vincent Lugert; vincent.lugert@lfulg.sachsen.de) requesting access and the lead investigator (Dr. Koushik Roy; kroy@frov.jcu.cz) providing the service via sharepoint online (shared cloud storage) folder named "AQUASERV PID 40871".

3. Where the data can be accessible and with what level of protection?
Answer: A restricted copy, with emabrgo to full access until a scientific publication occurs, will be made available online on ZENODO FFPW community with the title "AQUASERV PID 40871: xxxxxx" having publicly accessible doi number. Here all data will be gradually uploaded (for public access) from the sharepoint folder (for private access). It will ensure a permanent and traceable storage of project data. The fully publicly accesible and non-embargoed version in ZENODO FFPW community is expected not before 07.11.2026, that is one year after project ends, keeping ample time for a scientific publication to undergo drafting, submission, revision, and peer review. However, the page will be already active with partial data preview, and the data will be made available on request (privately).

4. Funding Acknowledgment.
Answer: In all data, metadata or video files and the scientific publication that will use the pellet as experimental feed, the "AQUASERV PID 40871" shall be duly acknowledged.

dmp.description:
The aim of the project  is to prepare "precision" seasonal pond feeds made of local, less-refined by-product/ co-product ingredients (mostly plant-based) that can resolve seasonal imbalances naturally happening in fishponds at the beginning or towards the end of the vegetative season to both natural food web and the nutrition of feeding fish in ponds. The aim will be achieved by following objectives:

1. To prepare water-stable pellets with sufficient integrity to withstand at least 3 hours of water stability, using circular ingredients.
2. To prepare biochemically precise pellets between analyzed values in the laboratory and planned values in feed formulation software.
3. To prepare pellets that are palatable by trained laboratory carp stocks.
